text: Any fool can write code that a computer can understand. Good programmers write code that humans can understand.
The best code is no code at all. Every new line of code you willingly bring into the world is code that has to be debugged.
First, solve the problem. Then, write the code. If you spend too long on the second step, you probably skipped the first.
Programming is not about typing, it is about thinking. The keyboard is just the tool you use to express what you have already solved in your mind.
Simplicity is prerequisite for reliability. If you cannot explain it simply, you do not understand it well enough to build it.
The most dangerous phrase in the language is: we have always done it this way. Question everything, even the foundations.
Talk is cheap. Show me the code. And make sure that code is clean, tested, and does exactly what it needs to do.
Code is like humor. When you have to explain it, it is bad. Write code so clear that it reads like well-written prose.
The function of good software is to make the complex appear to be simple. The user should never have to think about what is happening underneath.
Before software can be reusable it first has to be usable. Focus on making it work beautifully for one case before generalizing.
In a world obsessed with adding more features, the real skill is knowing what to leave out. Restraint is a superpower.
The computer was born to solve problems that did not exist before. Now it solves problems we did not even know we had.
Measuring programming progress by lines of code is like measuring aircraft building progress by weight. Less is often more.
A clever person solves a problem. A wise person avoids it entirely. The best engineers are the ones who delete code.
People think that computer science is the art of geniuses but the actual reality is the opposite, just many people doing things that build on each other.
The only way to go fast is to go well. Shortcuts today become roadblocks tomorrow. Take the time to do it right the first time.
It is not enough for code to work. Code that works but is messy will slow you down in ways you cannot predict or measure.
Perfection is achieved not when there is nothing more to add, but when there is nothing left to take away from the design.
The art of debugging is figuring out what you really told your computer to do rather than what you thought you told it to do.
Software is a great combination between artistry and engineering. When you finally get done and get to appreciate what you have built, it is like a series of sculptures.
The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog near the riverbank where wildflowers bloom in the warm light of the afternoon sun.
She opened the dusty notebook and found a letter she had written years ago but never sent, filled with words she no longer recognized as her own.
Thunder rolled across the darkening sky as the last train pulled away from the station, leaving nothing behind but silence and rain.
He walked through the market square where vendors shouted prices for fresh bread and ripe fruit while children chased pigeons between the stalls.
The lighthouse keeper climbed the spiral staircase each evening, carrying a lantern that flickered against the cold stone walls of the tower.
Between the mountains and the sea there was a narrow valley where the wind carried the scent of pine trees and salt water.
Maps had been drawn and redrawn a thousand times but the territory itself remained unchanged, indifferent to the names we gave it.
Somewhere between midnight and dawn the city finally goes quiet, and for a few hours the streets belong to the cats and the streetlights.
I do not fear computers. I fear the lack of them. A world without technology is a world without the tools to solve its greatest challenges.
Two things are infinite: the universe and human stupidity. And I am not sure about the universe. But I am quite sure about the other one.
In the middle of difficulty lies opportunity. The obstacle is not something to go around but something to go through and learn from.
The nitrogen in our DNA, the calcium in our teeth, the iron in our blood, the carbon in our apple pies were made in the interiors of collapsing stars.
We are all now connected by the internet, like neurons in a giant brain. The question is whether we will use that connection wisely.
Any sufficiently advanced technology is indistinguishable from magic. And every piece of magic was once just an idea someone refused to give up on.
I think the biggest innovations of the twenty-first century will be at the intersection of biology and technology. A new era is beginning.
Stay hungry, stay foolish. Your time is limited, so do not waste it living someone else's life. Follow your curiosity and intuition.
The internet is becoming the town square for the global village of tomorrow. Every voice matters, and every connection counts.
Do not judge each day by the harvest you reap but by the seeds that you plant. Progress is often invisible until it suddenly is not.
The only limit to our realization of tomorrow will be our doubts of today. Let us move forward with strong and active faith in what we build.
It is during our darkest moments that we must focus to see the light. Every setback is a setup for a comeback worth celebrating.
Life is what happens when you are busy making other plans. The best moments are the ones you did not schedule or expect.
In three words I can sum up everything I have learned about life: it goes on. And that simple truth is the most powerful one.
Debugging is twice as hard as writing the code in the first place. Therefore, if you write the code as cleverly as possible, you are by definition not smart enough to debug it.
There are only two hard things in computer science: cache invalidation, naming things, and off-by-one errors. That is three, which proves the point.
A program that produces incorrect results twice as fast is infinitely slower. Correctness always comes before performance optimization.
The most important property of a program is whether it accomplishes the intention of its user. Everything else is secondary to that.
Nine people cannot make a baby in one month. Some things take time and no amount of resources or parallelism can change that.
One of the best programming skills you can have is knowing when to walk away for a while. Fresh eyes find bugs faster than tired ones.
Weeks of coding can save you hours of planning. Always think before you type. The keyboard should be the last tool you reach for.
The goal of software engineering is to control complexity, not to create it. Every abstraction should make things simpler, never harder.
